# LUFA — minimal host-side HID reference (v1.6.0)

## What was taken, and why

| Kind | What | Where | Why |
|------|------|-------|-----|
| **Code (verbatim)** | Small subset of named HID constants: `HID_RI_*` masks/types/data sizes, `HID_IOF_*` flags, `HID_KEYBOARD_MODIFIER_*` masks, `HID_KEYBOARD_SC_*` scan codes | [`lufa_hid_constants.h`](lufa_hid_constants.h) | Gives the shipped USB HID check an independent, attributed source of truth for its 47 key codes and 8 modifier bits. Every identifier and value is LUFA's own. |
| **Idea (re-expressed in our style)** | LUFA's `HID_DESCRIPTOR_MOUSE` / `HID_DESCRIPTOR_KEYBOARD` canonical boot layouts: button bits then X/Y axes; keyboard = modifier byte + reserved byte + 6 key slots | [`lufa_hid_reference.h`](lufa_hid_reference.h) / [`.c`](lufa_hid_reference.c) — our own pure byte builders, tag block, our naming | Lets an existing shipped check actually **exercise the descriptor path**: generated bytes are fed to `components/usb/usb_hid_layout.c`, not to a second decoder. No LUFA preprocessor machinery, driver or parser is vendored. |
| **Not taken** | `HIDParser.c`, USB class drivers, AVR headers, demos, bootloaders, descriptor-macro encoders | — | LUFA is an AVR8 USB stack; it cannot run on the ESP32-P4 and would be a second USB stack. Nothing here is compiled into firmware or the ESP-IDF build. |

The integration is deliberately minimal: two small pure C files, one header of
verbatim constants, one host checker and one Python gate. No new firmware
module, no new USB path, no fixture generator duplicating existing tests.

## How it is actually used

`tools/thirdparty/lufa/lufa_hid_gate.py` compiles the checker **together with
the shipped decoder** (`components/usb/usb_hid_layout.c`) using
`gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror`, then runs it. The checker:

1. builds the canonical 58-byte mouse descriptor from the LUFA-derived idea
   and passes it to `usb_mouse_parse_layout()` — asserting field offsets and
   signed report extraction from the **production decoder**;
2. builds the canonical 64-byte keyboard descriptor and walks it to prove the
   modifier(8)/reserved(1)/keys(6) shape that `components/usb/usb.c` consumes;
3. compares the captured mouse fixture in `test/main/test_usb_hid_layout.c`
   byte-for-byte over its first 16 bytes (through the button count) with the
   generated canonical prefix, then decodes the whole fixture with the shipped
   decoder (including its wheel);
4. cross-checks all `USB_HID_KEY_*` / `USB_HID_MOD_*` defines in `usb.c`;
5. checks every shipped descriptor fixture is well-formed short-item HID.

Wiring: registered as `lufa` / `lufa_canary` in `tools/host_all_gates.py` and as
`LUFA HID constants` in `tools/harness/verify.py`. It runs in the shipped
board-free gate suite, fails loudly, and has a red canary with **four** tamper
cases: a key code, an item type, a button count and an axis width. Each must
make the gate return non-zero; a clean run must pass.

## Reproduction

From the repository root (no board, no serial port):

```powershell
python -m py_compile tools/thirdparty/lufa/lufa_hid_gate.py
gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -Itools/thirdparty/lufa -Icomponents/usb `
    tools/thirdparty/lufa/lufa_hid_fixture_check.c `
    tools/thirdparty/lufa/lufa_hid_reference.c `
    components/usb/usb_hid_layout.c -o "$env:TEMP\lufa_hid_check.exe"
& "$env:TEMP\lufa_hid_check.exe" components/usb/usb.c test/main/test_usb_hid_layout.c
python tools/thirdparty/lufa/lufa_hid_gate.py --check
python tools/thirdparty/lufa/lufa_hid_gate.py --self-test
python tools/host_all_gates.py --only lufa,lufa_canary
python tools/harness/verify.py
```

Why not firmware: the constraint was never flash (16 MB flash / 8 MB app is
ample); it is that LUFA is an AVR8-specific USB stack. On ESP32-P4 the single
USB path is the Espressif host component plus our own pure decoder. Porting
LUFA would add a second, incompatible USB driver and change the hardware
abstraction, so it stays host-only.
